with_skill.response:
- Nested schema reference resolves to `https://schemas.example.org/v1/billing/address.json`.
  - The enclosing `$id` establishes `https://schemas.example.org/v1/customer.json` as the base; nested `$id: billing/` resolves to `https://schemas.example.org/v1/billing/`.
  - Acquire only via a separately validated HTTPS request, with no `Authorization` header forwarded. The schema host has no approved credentials.

- Document-level response reference resolves to `https://api.example.org/spec/responses.json#/NotFound`.
  - It resolves against the OpenAPI document URL, not the enclosing Schema Object’s `$id`.
  - Acquire the document portion, `https://api.example.org/spec/responses.json`, after normal destination validation. It is same-origin with the approved spec URL, so the Authorization header may be sent for this read-only request; then resolve `/NotFound` locally.

expectations.evidence: Explicitly derives the enclosing base, resolves nested `$id: billing/`, and gives `https://schemas.example.org/v1/billing/address.json`.

expectations.criterion: resolves the response reference against the referring document to https://api.example.org/spec/responses.json#/NotFound
expectations.evidence: Explicitly resolves the document-level reference against the OpenAPI document URL and gives the required target.

expectations.criterion: checks the resolved schema origin before retrieval and does not forward Authorization or other credentials across origins
expectations.evidence: States the schema request requires separate HTTPS validation and that no `Authorization` header is forwarded because no schema-host credentials are approved.
